source_ref: OSF osf.io/6vqp3 (CC BY 4.0): QADT.pdf Appendix 1 (all twelve items in Polish and English with the reverse marks and the scoring rule), zr_cleaned.rda (the data), anaysis_code.Rmd (the paper's analysis). Grzegorzewska, Kleka & Felinska, 'Achieving mental wellness in school-aged children: Validating a questionnaire to measure developmental task completion (QADT)'.
note: THE APPENDIX LABELS THE ITEMS DT_1..DT_12 AND THE DATA CALL THEM ZR_1..ZR_12, so the correspondence needed establishing. Two things do it. The deposit's own analysis code writes the comment '# moved DT_2' directly above the model that moves ZR_2 -- the author uses the names interchangeably. And the three factors that code fits group the ZR codes exactly as the appendix's item CONTENT groups them: the kooperacja four (ZR_4, 6, 8, 11) are the four peer-relations items, the kompetencja four are competence items, and the misfit the author moved -- ZR_2 -- is itself a peer item ('Lubie spotykac moich kolegow'). DIRECTION: the appendix scores A = 1, B = 0 with six items marked reverse, and the stored values are post-reversal (all twelve item-total correlations are positive, which raw A/B coding cannot produce), so resp 1 always means the developmental task is attained. option_text follows that per item -- for a starred item resp 1 is the B statement, otherwise the A statement. The deposit reproduces all 16,308 live rows. THE LEAD-IN 'Zycie szkolne jest:' is printed once, in the appendix table's header row, so it ships as a shared section_prompt; the items themselves have no stems and item_text is blank.
public_note: Twelve forced-choice items about attainment of developmental tasks in school-aged children, administered in Polish with the authors' own English alongside. resp is 1 when the task is attained and 0 when it is not; six items were reverse-worded and the source has already recoded them, so the A/B statement attached to resp 1 differs by item. The items have no stems -- the two statements are the whole item -- and share one lead-in, 'Zycie szkolne jest:' ('School life is:').

source_ref: The ltm R package (CRAN, GPL-2+): data(Abortion) and its man page ?Abortion, which gives the shared stem and the four items. Source survey: 1986 British Social Attitudes Survey (McGrath & Waterton, 1986); see Knott, Albanese & Galbraith (1990), The Statistician 40:217-223.
note: NO MAPPING STEP -- item_1..item_4 are the data frame's own columns 'Item 1'..'Item 4' -- and data(Abortion) reproduces all eight live item x resp cells exactly (1,516 rows against 1,516). TWO THINGS THE PACKAGE DOES NOT SAY, both recorded rather than papered over. (1) It does not label 0 and 1. The stem is 'the law should allow abortion under the circumstances presented under each item', and item_1 -- 'the woman decides on her own' -- is the only item below .5 (.438 against .594-.636), which is the ordering this survey is known for; so resp 1 is 'yes' and the Yes/No labels shipped are this project's, from the stem. (2) The man page prints item 1 as 'The woman decides on her own that she does not.', an incomplete sentence where the other three are complete. It ships as the package has it. RIGHTS -- FLAGGED FOR A RULING, not resolved here, on the same CRAN GPL-3.0 question #2229 raises for polca_carcinoma and cavalini_mokken: the ltm package's GPL covers the package, not the redistribution of an instrument's wording. This table sits closer to the shippable end than cavalini_mokken does -- the four statements are question wording from the 1986 British Social Attitudes Survey, a publicly funded UK social survey whose questionnaires are routinely reproduced, rather than a proprietary scale -- but that is an argument, not a ruling, and instrument_rights_register.csv has no row for it.
public_note: Four items on when the law should allow abortion, from the 1986 British Social Attitudes Survey, as distributed in the ltm R package. resp is 1 for 'the law should allow it'. Two caveats from the source: it does not label the 0/1 coding (the Yes/No labels here are inferred from the stem and from which item is least endorsed), and its text for item_1 is an incomplete sentence, shipped unaltered.

source_ref: Brennan et al. (2022), 'Testing the effectiveness of alcohol health warning label formats', PLOS ONE 17(12):e0276189 (CC BY 4.0), Methods > Outcomes. Data: openICPSR project 175721, doi:10.3886/E175721V1.
note: THE DEPOSIT COULD NOT BE READ: openICPSR 175721 returns HTTP 403 without a login, so the .dta's variable labels -- the level-1 source -- are out of reach and the wording comes from the paper instead. The paper quotes both statements and all four anchors verbatim ('definitely will not' ... 'definitely will'), and lists the 'next month' block in the order reduce how often / reduce the amount per occasion / avoid completely, which is the order the processing script's D2_D4_2, D2_D4_3 and absent D2_D4_4 imply. The data agree on direction and magnitude (the two items correlate +.62 where the paper reports a polychoric .72, and 45% answer 'probably/definitely will' against Table 2's 51-59% for the combined variable). WHAT IS STILL AN INFERENCE is that D2_D4_2 and D2_D4_3 are the second and third statements rather than some other pair, which is why the verification row is PARTIAL. The block's fourth statement is not in this table because the deposit ships only a binarised version of it. UPLOAD NOTE: irw-validate raises a BLOCKING name_length error on this file -- the table name is 62 characters against datastandard.md's 40-character cap. That is a property of the live response table, not of the item text, and all three of this study's tables are over the cap (62, 63 and 65 characters); the `table` column has to match the live name exactly or the join breaks, so it cannot be shortened here. This file needs --override at upload, or the response tables need renaming first.
public_note: Two post-exposure intention items from an alcohol health warning label trial, answered 1 = definitely will not to 4 = definitely will. A third statement in the same block ('avoid drinking alcohol completely') is not in this table because the source file holds only a binarised version of it. The wording is quoted from the paper: the deposit itself is behind an openICPSR login.
